answer.skeleton: Heteroskedasticity (Var(u|x) varies with x) -> OLS still unbiased and consistent (exogeneity holds) -> standard errors wrong -> t-tests and CIs invalid -> OLS not BLUE, efficiency lost -> detect with residual plot, Breusch-Pagan (nR^2 ~ chi2(k)), White (adds squares and cross-products) -> remedies: keep OLS with robust sandwich SE (large-sample default; HC2/HC3 in small samples) or change the estimator: WLS with known h(x) (divide by sqrt(h)) or FGLS with estimated h (efficient only asymptotically, can hurt if h is misspecified) -> log transform as a possible fix of the variance pattern (mention only).

essential_core: Standard errors are wrong: invalid t-tests and CIs, too small in the spending example
OLS loses efficiency: Gauss-Markov needs homoskedasticity, so OLS is not BLUE
Robust sandwich SE: keep OLS, replace the middle term with the sum of squared residuals times x_i x_i'
WLS with known h(x): divide by sqrt(h(x)) to get a homoskedastic model
Breusch-Pagan: n times R^2 of squared residuals on regressors is chi-squared with k df under homoskedasticity
answer.order: Deep-study, general to specific: unbiasedness vs inference (SE wrong, doubt on why bias matters) -> efficiency loss -> detection (Breusch-Pagan, White) -> remedies (sandwich, WLS, FGLS) -> small-sample HC2/HC3 and the open WLS-vs-robust question.
